title: Longest Pause in US Boat Strikes Raises Doubts Southern Spear Curbed Cocaine Flow
detail: The US military went the longest stretch to date without a lethal strike on an alleged drug-trafficking vessel — no strikes since June 21, 2026 — prompting Pentagon and DEA officials to tell reporters that Operation Southern Spear has not meaningfully slowed cocaine entering the United States. Since the campaign began in September 2025, US forces have destroyed at least 67 vessels and killed at least 221 people in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific. US Southern Command chief Gen. Francis Donovan told lawmakers in March 2026 that 'boat strikes aren't the answer,' and analysts noted most cocaine still enters via land routes through Mexico and via shipping containers rather than small boats. Trump administration officials maintain the campaign has 'virtually ended' seaborne trafficking, a claim Pentagon and DEA analysts dispute.
